fields.meta_title: Donation Form Builder With a Donor Database | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a donation form from a prompt: monthly gifts, in-kind drop-offs, tribute cards, and receipts for gifts of $250 or more. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Donation Form for Every Kind of Gift
fields.hero_description: Build a donation form that takes one-time and monthly gifts and saves every donor to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Happens After a Donor Clicks Give
fields.features_subheading: To a donor, one donation form looks like another. The difference is what gets built behind the page and who owns it.
fields.feature_1:
A form written from your gift policy

Describe the gifts you accept and who should hear about the large ones. Emergent builds the form and its donor tables, then changes either one each time you prompt again.
fields.feature_2:
Card gifts through your own Stripe account

Connects to the Stripe account the charity already uses, or another processor with an API. Each completed gift saves to the form's records with its amount and the fund it supports.
fields.feature_3:
Donors and gifts in a database you own

Saves each donor once and each gift as its own row in a database you own. A donor's third gift joins the same history, and the tables sync to HubSpot or any CRM with an API.
fields.feature_4:
Large gifts reach a person the same day

Sends an email or Slack message to the development lead when a gift passes the amount you set, with past gifts attached. A reminder follows if no thank-you is logged by morning.
fields.feature_5:
No cap on gifts in a year-end push

Takes the last gift on December 31 the same way it took the first one in January. The form has no response cap, and nothing closes when a campaign does better than the plan said.
fields.feature_6:
The form's code in your GitHub

Exports the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A volunteer developer can add a fund or a field in code, and the next person to run development inherits all of it.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Kinds of Gift and the Rule Behind Each
fields.tab_content_1:
$40 every month, and the $1.20 card fee on top

Kestrel Point Literacy Project's form opens on monthly giving, with presets of $20, $40, and $80. Vivienne Szabo picks $40 and ticks the box to cover the $1.20 card fee. Each month on the same day, $41.20 goes through the Stripe account the project connects, and her row in the donors table holds the next billing date.
fields.tab_content_2:
Coats in sizes the shelter is still short on

Corwin Street Family Shelter's coat drive form lists only the sizes still on the needs list. Kids medium is short 14 coats, and the full adult sizes no longer appear. Marisol Ventura pledges 5 kids medium coats and books the Tuesday 4:00 PM drop-off, which puts her on coordinator Hollis Oduya's list.
fields.tab_content_3:
A tribute card with no dollar amount on it

Rosalind Feeney gives $75 to Alder Crest Hospice Foundation in memory of Walt Aldington and names his daughter, June Aldington, as the person to tell. June gets an emailed card that names Rosalind and the tribute. The amount stays off the card and on the gift record, where the $75 counts toward the memorial fund.
fields.tab_content_4:
Every gift of $250 or more gets a written receipt

The IRS describes a written acknowledgment for a charitable contribution of $250 or more. One item it lists is a statement that no goods or services were provided, if that is the case. Westmoor Arts Collective's form emails that receipt as soon as Callum Theroux's $300 gift goes through. A copy saves to his donor record.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Donation Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build a donation form that takes monthly gifts and sends receipts, tested on five gifts before it goes live.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the gift the form asks for first
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 List the fields the receipt needs
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide whether the page leads with a one-time or a monthly gift, then set three preset amounts from your recent gifts. A program whose typical gift is $50 might offer $25, $50, and $100, with an open amount field below them.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write down what the thank-you and the receipt need, which comes down to the donor's contact details and the gift itself. Cut any field that feeds neither one. A phone field nobody calls is one more box between the donor and the button.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Link the Stripe account that gifts go through now, or any other processor that has an API. Gifts keep landing in the account your bookkeeper reconciles today, and the form reads each completed payment back into its own records.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Brief Emergent the way you would brief a new volunteer: the presets and the monthly default, plus who hears about a gift over $1,000. Emergent builds the form and the tables behind it, along with a dashboard the development staff can open each morning.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Write the receipt and the thank-you
fields.howto_step_5_des: Draft the receipt wording with whoever signs your gift acknowledgments, including the line about any goods or services given in return. Write a separate thank-you for monthly donors that tells them the next billing date and how to change the amount.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run five test gifts before launch: one-time, monthly, a tribute, one with the fee box ticked, and one at $250 or more. Check that each lands in the right table and that every email reads the way you wrote it.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Publish and watch the first week
fields.howto_step_7_des: Put the form on the donate page and link it from your next email appeal. Read the donors table each morning for the first week, and swap out a preset amount if almost nobody picks it.

faq_plan.a: A donation form is the page or paper form a charity uses to take a gift and record who gave it and how much. Online, it also hands the payment to a processor and starts the receipt and thank-you that follow.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a donation form?
faq_plan.ref: How do I create a donation form?

prov.original: How do I create a donation form?

faq_plan.a: Describe it in plain English in Emergent's AI form builder: the preset amounts, whether monthly comes first, and what should happen after each gift. Emergent then builds the form along with the donor records it writes to. Connect your payment processor, send a few test gifts, and then share the link.

faq_plan.q: Can you provide some examples of donation request forms?
faq_plan.ref: Can you provide some examples of donation request forms?

prov.original: Can you provide some examples of donation request forms?

faq_plan.a: Yes. A donation request form runs the other way from a gift form: a group uses it to ask a business for support. Examples include a restaurant's form for gift card requests from school auctions and a grocer's form for food drive help. A business that fields these requests can post donation forms on its own site, one per request type, and get the same details every time.

faq_plan.q: How do I embed a crypto donation form on a nonprofit website?
faq_plan.ref: how to embed crypto donation form nonprofit website
faq_plan.a: If your crypto giving provider offers an embed code, paste it into an HTML or embed block on the donate page, beside the card form, not in place of it. Make a small test gift and confirm it reaches the right wallet. The same embed step puts any other form on the site, such as an employee information form in a staff portal.

faq_plan.q: How do you choose a top-rated online donation form?
faq_plan.ref: how do you choose a top-rated online donation form
faq_plan.a: Choose the online donation form that donors finish, not the one with the longest feature list. Try it on a phone, count the fields before the amount, and check that switching to monthly takes one tap. Then ask where the gifts are stored. On Emergent, the form you build keeps each gift in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What should a donation form template include?
faq_plan.a: A donation form template should include preset amounts with an open field, a one-time or monthly choice, contact details for the receipt, and the fund or campaign. Add a tribute option and a fee-cover box only if someone will act on them. Put the amount before the contact fields, since the amount is the decision the donor came to make.

faq_plan.q: Is a fundraising form the same as a donation form?
faq_plan.a: No. A donation form takes a gift, while a fundraising form can also register runners, sell event tickets, or record pledges toward a goal. A charity run can pair its registration with a liability waiver form that each runner signs before race day.

faq_plan.q: Can I make a free donation form?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent is free to start, and its free tier covers building and publishing a free donation form with the donor database behind it. Before launch, look up the per-gift fee of the card processor you connect, and add a cover-the-fee box if you want donors to have the option.

prov.original: Can you provide an example of a donation request form?

flagged: PA10 shared with a sibling page
faq_plan.a: Here is one: a hardware store's donation request form for community projects. It asks for the group's name and tax ID, then the project date. Next come the materials needed and who will collect them. The form also states the store's rule that requests arrive 4 weeks ahead. A donation form PDF covers the same fields for groups that mail their requests.

faq_plan.q: How to draft a donation form?
faq_plan.ref: How to draft a donation form?

prov.original: How to draft a donation form?

faq_plan.a: Draft it on paper before you build anything, one line per field, in the order a donor meets them. Start with the amount, then frequency, then name and contact, then payment. Then read it the way you would review an intake form: every question needs a reason someone on staff will act on.
